newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria revokes Ashland oil licences.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria revokes Ashland oil licences.

text.p: Nigeria said on Friday that oil minister Dan Etete had ordered the revocation of four oil prospecting licences (OPLS) awarded to Ashland Oil Company, a subsidiary of Ashland Corp.

"This revocation order has become necessary because Ashland sold its rights and interests in the OPLs without seeking the written consent of the government as required by law," a statement from the oil ministry in the capital Abuja said.
The four OPLs and were signed in 1973 and 1991 under production sharing contracts by which Ashland bears the costs of exploration and recovers its expenses if oil is struck.
An oil ministry official said he believed the four licences were all that Ashland, a relatively smaller oil operator in Nigeria, held in the West African country.
The statement said Ashland sold its interests in the OPLs to Perenco Investments S.A., adding "This transaction is not only against the law of the land, it is against our national interest."
It said despite Etete's intervention emphasing the need for official consent, Ashland went ahead with the transactions.

"This reached a climax when two representatives of Perenco Investment S.A. met with the honourable minister confirming the sales and Ashland also corroborated the sales by its letter of June 12, 1997 faxed to the honourable minister," it added.
The statement also said all work permits and expatriate quota granted Ashland based on their oil business in Nigeria had been revoked and withdrawn.
No one was immediately available at Ashland's Lagos office to comment and a telephone operator said management staff were holding "an important meeting."
